---
title: "DLMAX"
subtitle: "Dynamic Linear Models in JAX"
jupyter: python3
---

DLMAX provides an implementation of the @west_harrison_1997 Bayesian dynamic linear model (DLM) for time series forecasting. We start with the fundamental assumption that model parameters and model form are uncertain, but that we can learn something about both from observed data. The DLM deals mostly with model-level parameters, and is augmented by a dynamic model averaging framework (DMA) [@raftery_dma_2010].

This approach means that rather than committing to a single model, DLMAX filters a whole *universe* of
candidate models (combinations of level, trend, seasonal and discount settings) in parallel and combines their forecasts — weighting each model by its recent predictive performance, so the blend adapts over time.

Both modelling approaches are fundamentally *sequential* in nature, meaning that new data is processed *once* post-observation, and we avoid endless, wasteful re-fitting of old data.

The models are exposed through a high-level API and implemented in JAX for vectorised, device-parallel filtering.


::: {.callout-note}
## Alpha release

`v0.1.0`. The numerics are tested and stable, but this is a `0.x` release and
the public API may change between minor versions
([semver](https://semver.org/#spec-item-4)) — pin an exact version if you
depend on it. Bug reports and questions are welcome via
[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/ross-h1/DLMAX/issues).
:::

## Installation

```bash
pip install awen-dlmax
```

The distribution is published as **`awen-dlmax`**; the import name is
`DLMAX`.

DLMAX requires 64-bit floats. Enable them once at process start:

```python
from DLMAX import enable_x64
enable_x64()  # or set JAX_ENABLE_X64=1 in the environment
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# Setup for the executed examples: 64-bit floats, quiet import noise, chart theme.
import os
os.environ["TQDM_DISABLE"] = "1"
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from DLMAX import enable_x64
enable_x64()
import seaborn as sns
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="notebook")
```

## Input format

Series are supplied as a pandas DataFrame in either shape, detected
automatically and giving identical results.

**Long** — one row per observation, columns `(unique_id, ds, y)`: the series
name, the timestamp (or an integer index), and the observation. Series may
differ in length and need not share a calendar.

**Wide** — one row per period: the index is the timestamp, each column is a
series, and the column names are the series ids. A series that starts late or
ends early is `NaN` in those cells, and missing values are carried through the
filter as missing rather than imputed.

Wide input is converted to long internally, and forecasts come back keyed the
way the input was.

## Quick start

Load the bundled airline-passengers series and forecast 24 months ahead:

```{python}
from DLMAX import AutoFFS, load_dataset

df = load_dataset("airline_passengers")          # 144 monthly obs, long format
forecast = AutoFFS(season_length=12).forecast(df, h=24, level=[80, 95])
forecast.head()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-quickstart
#| fig-cap: "AutoFFS 24-month forecast with 80% and 95% prediction intervals."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
sns.lineplot(data=df, x="ds", y="y", color="0.35", label="history", ax=ax)
sns.lineplot(data=forecast, x="ds", y="AutoFFS", color="C0", label="forecast", ax=ax)
for lo, hi, alpha in [("AutoFFS-lo-95", "AutoFFS-hi-95", 0.15),
                      ("AutoFFS-lo-80", "AutoFFS-hi-80", 0.25)]:
    ax.fill_between(forecast["ds"], forecast[lo], forecast[hi], color="C0", alpha=alpha)
ax.set(xlabel="", ylabel="passengers")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

Input is long-format: a DataFrame with `unique_id`, `ds`, `y` columns —
exactly what [`load_dataset`](reference/load_dataset.qmd) returns. The same model
also supports persistent `fit` / `predict` / `update` and a single-pass
`cross_validation` backtest — see [Three ways to use it](#three-ways-to-use-it)
below.

## Three ways to use it

- **Persistent** — [`fit`](reference/AutoFFS.qmd) once, then
  [`predict`](reference/AutoFFS.qmd) / [`update`](reference/AutoFFS.qmd)
  repeatedly. Each datapoint is filtered exactly once; ideal for sequential or
  streaming use.
- **Stateless** — [`forecast`](reference/AutoFFS.qmd) runs a one-shot fit +
  predict, for when the state is not needed afterwards.
- **Backtest** — [`cross_validation`](reference/AutoFFS.qmd) emits rolling-origin
  forecasts from a single forward pass.

For very large panels with series entering and leaving over time, see
[`AutoFFSUniverse`](reference/AutoFFSUniverse.qmd), which manages a persistent,
length-batched universe on disk. The lower-level
[`uv_dlm`](reference/uv_dlm.qmd) and
[`multi_model_dlm`](reference/multi_model_dlm.qmd) classes expose the underlying
filter directly.

See the [API Reference](reference/index.qmd) for the full public API.
